purpose.summary: Resolve cold native chainstate prevouts outside validation locks through owned snapshots and copied cache overlays, while retaining the existing upstream Chronik indexer and closed daemon admission.
scope: Add native owned LevelDB and coin read sessions that retain the database, snapshot, key and storage resources independently of the wrapper. Existing native read/write and coin serialization rules remain unchanged.

Copy actual mempool parents and cache entries, including spent tombstones, under both native fences. Resolve cold native keys and convert pool entries after release, without borrowing pcoinsTip or its backend.
Recheck chain/pool generations plus cache/database owners before applying and before publication; discard races and quarantine stable contradictions only in the index.

Retain all 39 earlier native cases and add five owned/cold-chainstate cases. Require six disjoint groups with 44 cases and 2285 assertions per repetition, ten repetitions, fixed 60-second process limits and verified cleanup.
Keep the original upstream/donor manifests and ERGON-CHANGE-0045 record byte-identical. Add a separate finite layer of 13 technical and seven policy paths over the public PR #51 checkpoint.
The parent is a public review branch, not an assumed accepted main revision. Landing requires acceptance of the parent and a renewed exact binding if the accepted parent differs.
exclusions: No daemon startup/reindex hook, activation, operator-server access, deployment, cutover, release, merge or desktop integration.
No token algorithm, consensus, chain selection, economic/network parameter, wallet, plugin or dependency changes.
No incoming evidence, binary, generated output, cache, datadir, private history or host metadata.

commands: Build bitcoind and test_bitcoin with both upstream flags and BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF in the separate compiled-out CI matrix job. Run the isolated 0-to-3 zero-subsidy regtest mining and positive-stop smoke.
expected_results: Native mining and shutdown work without linking Rust/Chronik; no Chronik state or external peer connection is created.

commands: Retain the older observer CI profile unchanged. Separately build the actual upstream stack with BUILD_CHRONIK_UPSTREAM_LINK=ON, archival fixtures enabled and BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF; mine and stop without any runtime opt-in.
expected_results: The two optional profiles are never combined. Upstream linking alone creates no daemon Chronik runtime, database or listener.

commands: Run the source layer, preserved host/donor gates and their standard-library self-tests; build the archival profile with Rust 1.93.1 and repeat all six exact native groups ten times (44 cases / 2285 assertions per repetition, 60 fresh processes). Retain the older observer matrices as distinct controls.
expected_results: The earlier 39 cases remain selected. Five new native cases cover owned snapshot lifetime/decoding, file-backed cold reads, spent cache overlays, owner/ABA rejection and positive reader shutdown with native progress. No claim transfers from the older observer to the new upstream profile.

scenarios.command: Run the six exact upstream groups via run_repetitions.py repeat, including the five owned/cold-chainstate cases (file-backed native DB reads outside both fences). Retain the existing observer-profile canaries separately; they are not upstream service evidence.
expected_results: Exact 44 cases / 2285 assertions per repetition; stable normalized commitments and cleanup across 60 fresh processes.
Cold reads do not fill the native cache; spent overlays never fall back to the database. Old source/cache/DB owner captures cannot publish Ready.
Positive Stop joins paused readers while native validation still progresses; stable fixture contradictions quarantine only the index.
failure_conditions: Borrowed native cache/DB ownership after release; cold database Get under either native lock; lost spent tombstone; stale source/owner publication; partial Ready; native shutdown; skip, wrong selection/count, instability, timeout, nonzero exit or incomplete cleanup.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Restart the HTTP canary node and compare the exact confirmed Tx bytes; run the retained-window observer restart scenario. Separately exercise upstream owned startup and database reopen in the fixture-only profile, including a nonempty parent/child mempool.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Confirmed bytes remain identical after restart and no orphan or unbound response is served.
failure_conditions: Restart drift, stale query, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run the two-role pruning canary with fresh-pruned bootstrap and concurrent requests during already-indexed pruning.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.

Concurrent old-transaction reads are either canonical 200 or protobuf 503, never a fabricated or partial response. After file removal the old transaction is 503; a retained recent transaction remains 200 and the node continues at its accepted height.
The pre-existing fresh-pruned observer bootstrap failure remains isolated from node correctness.
failure_conditions: Silent 404 for an indexed pruned transaction, fabricated fallback, partial result, node shutdown, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex. Separately exercise upstream retained-anchor and source-generation contradictions; the fixture observer closes while native progress continues.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: The public review parent is PR #51 head, not assumed origin/main acceptance. Rebind and rerun if the accepted parent differs before landing.
Open Question / record-review-only, empty public artifacts. Local tests and CI do not automatically establish independent reproduction or service readiness.
Native storage/cache APIs are always built. Only the separate opt-in adapter uses this new session; existing native consensus/validation reads and writes are unchanged.

A LevelDB snapshot plus copied native cache overlay is coherent only under the native source fence and native cache/flush discipline. Snapshot acquisition is metadata-only; file-backed Get does not claim an OS page-cache miss or physical disk latency.
Owned readers can retain native database file locks. Positive reader shutdown is required before native storage reopen/reindex; no daemon lifecycle hook is introduced by this change.

Unpruned bounded regtest fixtures only: height <= 2000, pool <= 4096 entries, retained 288 blocks/transient 576 and raw payload <= 64 MiB. Total RSS, chain-height scaling and production resource budgets remain unproved.
Earlier observer pruning/reindex canaries remain separate; their results do not establish those behaviors for the upstream-linked service.
Positive joins can wait for stalled storage; there is no formal concurrency proof or production shutdown deadline.
The 344-package Rust closure remains unchanged. System dependencies, SDK and CI runner are not fully locked; source/CMake binding is not binary-to-source provenance.
No native consensus tokens, plugin migration, mainnet replay, operator database compatibility, packaging, deployment or cutover claim.
counterevidence: A const CCoinsViewCache read can fetch from disk and mutate the cache: simply releasing locks around pcoinsTip is unsafe.
An older unspent DB value may coexist with a dirty spent cache tombstone. Cache absence and spent presence must never be conflated.
The same tip hash and unchanged generations do not identify a replacement native cache owner; an owned nonreusable identity and DB lease are required.
Native chain ABA or pool drift invalidates detached inputs even if bytes or final tip hashes appear equal.
Keeping a database alive is not permission to race storage reopen; the real file lock persists until the final owned reader releases it.
Bounded regtest/source-gate success does not replace independent review, integrated CI, actual service lifecycle testing or public reproduction.
